t:
The Emergency Rail Services Act of 1970 is amended—

    (1) 
in section 2 (45 U.S.C. 661)—

        (A) 
by striking paragraph (2) and inserting in lieu thereof the following:


“(2) 
‘Board’ means the Surface Transportation Board.”; and



 
        (B) 
in paragraph (3) by striking “common carrier by railroad subject to part I of the Interstate Commerce Act (49 U.S.C. 1–27)” and inserting in lieu thereof “rail carrier subject to part A of subtitle IV of title 49, United States Code”;
  
    (2) 
in section 3—

        (A) 
by striking “the provisions of section 5 of the Interstate Commerce Act” in subsection (b)(4) and inserting in lieu thereof “subchapter II of chapter 113 of title 49, United States Code”; and
 
        (B) 
by striking “Commission” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”; and
  
    (3) 
in section 6(a) (45 U.S.C. 665(a)) by striking “Interstate Commerce Commission” and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”.

fable.w: This section only makes conforming amendments to the Emergency Rail Services Act of 1970, substituting the Surface Transportation Board for the Interstate Commerce Commission and updating cross-references. The tempting reading is that mention of a "Board" signals an advisory body, but the Surface Transportation Board is a federal agency and the text creates no process involving anyone outside the federal government. It provides for no comment period, hearing, consultation, rulemaking or right to sue.
fable.s: by striking “Commission” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments updating statutory references from the defunct Interstate Commerce Commission to the Surface Transportation Board. It does not establish any new process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The changes are purely administrative and internal to the federal government's regulatory structure.
qwen_block.s: The Emergency Rail Services Act of 1970 is amended— (1) in section 2 (45 U.S.C. 661)— (A) by striking paragraph (2) and inserting in lieu thereof the following: “(2) ‘Board’ means the Surface Transportation Board.”; and (B) in paragraph (3) by striking “common carrier by railroad subject to part I of the Interstate Commerce Act (49 U.S.C. 1–27)” and inserting in lieu thereof “rail carrier subject to part A of subtitle IV of title 49, United Code”; (2) in section 3— (A) by striking “the provisions of section 5 of the Interstate Commerce Act” in subsection (b)(4) and inserting in lieu thereof “subchapter II of chapter 113 of title 49, United States Code”; and (B) by striking “Commission” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”; and (3) in section 6(a) (45 U.S.C. 665(a)) by striking “Interstate Commerce Commission” and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”.

opus.w: This section only makes conforming amendments. It swaps references to the Interstate Commerce Commission for the Surface Transportation Board and updates statutory citations. The mention of a 'Board' and 'rail carrier' might look like regulatory process, but the section gives outside parties no consultation, hearing, comment, advisory, or litigation role in any federal decision. It also grants no new rulemaking authority, so no participation is recommended or required.
opus.s: by striking “Commission” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”
opus.b:
**Step 1. Reasoning.** It's tempting to read this as participation because it mentions a "Board" and "rail carrier[s]", which sounds like a regulatory body and the outside companies it oversees. That reading fails. These are only technical conforming amendments: they redefine "Board" as the Surface Transportation Board, update citations to the Interstate Commerce Act, and replace "Commission" with "Board". Nothing here creates a consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government.

**Step 2. Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments updating statutory references and definitions to reflect the transition from the Interstate Commerce Commission to the Surface Transportation Board. It does not create any new requirements for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The changes are purely administrative and legalistic, affecting internal statutory consistency rather than establishing a participatory process for non-federal actors.
qwen_chat.s: The Emergency Rail Services Act of 1970 is amended— (1) in section 2 (45 U.S.C. 661)— (A) by striking paragraph (2) and inserting in lieu thereof the following: “(2) ‘Board’ means the Surface Transportation Board.”; and (B) in paragraph (3) by striking “common carrier by railroad subject to part I of the Interstate Commerce Act (49 U.S.C. 1–27)” and inserting in lieu thereof “rail carrier subject to part A of subtitle IV of title 49, United Code”; (2) in section 3— (A) by striking “the provisions of section 5 of the Interstate Commerce Act” in subsection (b)(4) and inserting in lieu thereof “subchapter II of chapter 113 of title 49, United States Code”; and (B) by striking “Commission” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”; and (3) in section 6(a) (45 U.S.C. 665(a)) by striking “Interstate Commerce Commission” and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text references the "Surface Transportation Board" and "rail carriers," it involves outside parties. However, the text itself is purely technical, updating statutory cross-references and definitions to reflect the renaming of the Interstate Commerce Commission to the Surface Transportation Board. It does not establish any new process for public comment, consultation, or advisory input. The actors mentioned (the Board, rail carriers) are either federal agencies or regulated entities, but the section does not mandate any interaction between them that constitutes participation in a decision-making process as defined (e.g., no hearings, no advisory committees with outside members, no consultation requirements). The changes are administrative updates to legal citations.
